blockers: Both 'confirmed' and 'penalty' headline claims rest on a calibration gate passed only by pooling. The preregistration gates 'per model and set' (exps/c2_confirm/PREREGISTRATION.md:18). The haiku union passes (solve 0.206) only by averaging the contest set (0.71, n=24) with the arXiv set (0.05, n=79), which fails the gate on its own (exps/c2_confirm/results.txt, haiku_conf/haiku_repl; AMENDMENTS.md:19-21). The arXiv set supplies 77% of problems and drives both effects. On the gate-passing contest set alone, H1 D = 0.00 [-0.125, +0.125], and H2 = +0.125 rests on 3 of 24 non-zero problems (raw p 0.043, which would not survive Holm). Contribution (1) ('a penalty on held-out problems beyond it', paper/main.tex:30) and the abstract's 'confirmed' H2 (main.tex:19) therefore come from a set the authors' own rule says not to interpret. Either restate both as non-confirmatory, or rerun with a gate-passing held-out set of adequate size.

The competence account of the penalty (main.tex:19, 67, 87) is post hoc (exps/posthoc/solvability_split.py:1-6). It is also not the only reading of the evidence. Pooled over screen and held-out problems there is no overall penalty: D = +0.06, 95% CI [-0.01, +0.13] (exps/posthoc/solvability_split.json 'all'). My split by source shows that the 105-problem 'unsolved' stratum is 74 arXiv problems. Its direction does recur in screen unsolved (+0.125, n=24) and contest unsolved (+0.14, n=7), but those strata are too small to support claims. The abstract leads with this as a finding ('suggests the penalty appears beyond competence'), which overstates exploratory evidence.

Positioning and originality. A target-absent pool with a NONE option is a none-of-the-above/abstention multiple-choice setting, and the paper never positions against that literature. Examples: Kadavath et al. 2022, which tests none-of-the-above options (https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.05221), and the LLM abstention survey of Wen et al. 2024 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.18418). Related work (main.tex:33-35) cites only a workshop paper and a COLING paper for listwise judging. As written, the novelty claimed in contributions (1)-(2) cannot be assessed against the known result that models over-select when no option is right.
non_blocking: H2 ('forced pick selects the candidate the same model's verification passes most', main.tex:71) is expected under any model in which one latent plausibility score drives both formats, so calling it a 'failure' oversells it. The practical recommendation to use 'a verifier other than the selector' (main.tex:87) is untested: no cross-model verifier arm exists in exps/c2_confirm.

FORCED is not actually forced. In 31 of 103 haiku held-out FORCED replies, the model first states that none of the candidates is correct and then emits a CHOICE (e.g., exps/c2_confirm/raw/haiku__FORCED__aime_2026_10_TA.json). That reply is scored as a pick in H2 (exps/c2_confirm/analyze.py:72-77). Report this and run H2 excluding those replies as a sensitivity check.

'Unique winner in 90% of TA pools' (abstract; main.tex:70) mostly follows from the round-robin format with 3 candidates: the TA and TP tie rates are both 0.10 (exps/screens/s3_tournament/results.txt). Only the AUROC of 0.56 [0.47, 0.65] is informative, so lead with it.

Scope is thin for a flagship venue. There is one interpretable subject (haiku): sonnet failed its gate, and its cost cap was exceeded (AMENDMENTS.md:15-16). The data are one vendor, one day, math final answers only, and about 100 held-out problems. Seven exploratory screens (main.tex:74) dilute the paper and would be better in an appendix.

ISO uses 3 calls per pool and PICK uses 1 (main.tex:45). This biases toward finding ISO >= PICK, so the observed penalty is conservative in that respect. Still, report a per-call-matched comparison (for example, ISO on one random candidate rescaled), since it affects how D is interpreted.

Reproducibility of the reported numbers is good. I recomputed H1 (+0.1165, n=103) and H2 (+0.1165, n=103; the equal values are a coincidence: H1 counts 18/6 discordant, H2 counts 12 at 1.0, 9 at 0.5, 7 at -0.5, 1 at -1.0) from exps/c2_confirm/raw with my own parser, and both match results/claims.json. The study is honestly reported, with killed hypotheses kept in the ledger.

Calibration: per my instructions I did not read reviews/calibration*.json, so this score is anchored to the stated 1-10 scale, not to the calibration median. The work is careful and honest but makes a small, partly non-confirmatory contribution on one small model. I would place it at workshop level.
